# AzureDeck 2.0.0

Major launch reliability overhaul:
- Centralized account launch/rejoin queue, duplicate prevention, four bounded workers and adaptive startup overlap. Native starts remain exclusive and at least five seconds apart.
- Cached Roblox deployment/channel checks, complete installation discovery, validated direct launch and supported launcher fallback.
- Automatic shared maintenance waits for active sessions and existing updater work before changing installation files. It updates first, then uses a bounded reinstall if needed. Healthy sessions are preserved; unfinished accounts remain saved after unrecoverable installation failures.
- Per-account recoverable failures use bounded exponential backoff. Startup timeout, concurrency and pacing are configurable under Launch & recovery.
- Encrypted unfinished work resumes after restart, with retry counts and completion records. Cancellation works even while the queue is paused.
- Rotating structured diagnostics record launch versions, PIDs, outcomes and recovery decisions without credentials or command lines.

Existing account/group/browser/Discord/macros/graphics/config controls remain available. Update from Settings > App updates.

Validation uses synthetic accounts and controlled disposable processes, including fifty queued accounts, concurrent admission and restart recovery. Real 30–50 account game sessions, live private-server/Discord behavior and Roblox Home logout at high account counts are not claimed verified. Maintenance stays queued if active sessions never finish; Roblox can still require updates and Windows security prompts remain in force. Read the repository's VALIDATION.md and docs/RELEASE-2.0.0.md for full evidence and limits.
